goals: Understand the 35 CASH payment and 2 CASH fee
Understand what duties remain after the partial payment
Distinguish source funding from the proposed full-backing policy

actions.action: Clicked “Inspect the invoice worksheet” from the hero.
actions.observed: The page navigated to #worksheet. A fresh context started with Seller payment 35, Source behavior selected, escrow funding 110, seller receipt 35, fee recipient receipt 2, cash remaining 73, invoice duty 65, reserve duty 10, and total duties 75.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: the 35 payment reduces the 100 invoice duty to 65; the separate 10 reserve duty remains, so total duties are 75. The 2 fee does not pay down the invoice. In source mode the resulting 73 CASH is 2 below the 75 duties.
evidence: Supplied worksheet screenshot shows 112 proposed funding, unlike the fresh browser default; see finding F01.

actions.action: Focused Seller payment and used Home then 41 ArrowRight key presses to change it from 35 to 42.
actions.observed: The live values updated to seller receives 42, fee recipient receives 2, cash remaining 66, invoice duty 58, reserve duty 10, total duties 68; source funding stayed 110 and the worksheet displayed a 2 CASH backing gap. Gross escrow debit was 44.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: moving the slider makes clear that the fee does not discharge invoice duty, and the remaining duties track the unpaid invoice plus reserve.

actions.observed: For the 42 payment, funding changed to 112, cash remaining became 68, and total duties remained 68. The page says the extra 2 is an assumption beyond source open, S12 has no extra-funding action, and later partials need another fee allowance.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: I understand 112 as a proposed one-partial funding policy that adds 2 to cover the partial fee; it is not what the source action does.

actions.action: Opened “Exact asset, opening costs & lifecycle limits.”
actions.observed: The disclosure says CASH is the S12 fixture asset and not a Cardano asset; source open transfers 110 and charges a separate 3 CASH opening fee, for gross buyer debit 113. It also says the reserve duty remains and Close stays blocked under the proposed 112 policy, and later partials need more fee allowance.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful for understanding the separate opening fee and why the reserve survives; this detail is below the worksheet and must be opened.

actions.action: Opened the page question “Can S12 fund the escrow with 112?”
actions.observed: The answer says 112 is a proposed application policy; S12 open funds face plus reserve and has no extra transfer, and only non-negative custody is enforced.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: directly answered whether the 112 amount is an existing source action (it is not).
evidence: Visible FAQ answer “Can S12 fund the escrow with 112?”

actions.action: Clicked “Explore a Web” and read the A Web and A Strand explanations; opened “What is a Strand?” and “Does restoring a Strand verify the Web?”
actions.observed: The page calls a Web a proposed script-bound collection of Strands required by a consuming contract for one transition. A Strand is an individual proof with its claim, statement, and binding metadata. The FAQ says illustrated roles are not proof verification, acceptance, or settlement.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful for my teach-back: it defines the terms while clearly marking this site’s examples as illustrations.
evidence: FAQ answers “What is a Strand?” and “Does restoring a Strand verify the Web?”

questions.question: After the example payment of 35 CASH and the 2 CASH fee, what remains owed?
questions.whereItArose: Worksheet shows seller receives 35 and fee recipient receives 2.
questions.answerLocation: Worksheet totals: invoice duty 65, reserve duty 10, total duties 75; nearby note says only the seller payment discharges invoice duty and the fee does not.
questions.remainingClarification: None for the one partial shown.

questions.question: Does S12 itself provide the 112 CASH funding, or is 112 a proposed change?
questions.whereItArose: Worksheet screenshot starts at proposed funding 112, while the fresh interactive page starts at source funding 110.
questions.answerLocation: Worksheet note and FAQ “Can S12 fund the escrow with 112?” say 112 is a proposed policy, not an S12 action; the source only enforces non-negative custody.
questions.remainingClarification: The supplied worksheet screenshot should identify that it shows the proposed state because it differs from the fresh browser default.

questions.question: Is the 2 CASH partial fee added to the 35 CASH payment, and is there also an opening fee?
questions.whereItArose: Worksheet separates Seller receives from Fee recipient receives and states gross escrow debit; the buyer opening cost is not in the main arithmetic card.
questions.answerLocation: Worksheet says gross escrow debit is 37 CASH for a 35 payment plus 2 fee. Open “Exact asset, opening costs & lifecycle limits” to find that source open separately charges the buyer 3 CASH and gives gross opening debit 113.
questions.remainingClarification: None after opening the disclosure; the 3 CASH opening fee is easy to miss if the reader only sees the green worksheet card.

findings.impact: A payer comparing the supplied section screenshot with the live worksheet can think the starting funding amount changed or that 112 is the source default.
findings.observation: The supplied worksheet screenshot shows “PROPOSED full-backing policy” selected with Escrow funding 112 CASH at the 35 payment. In a fresh isolated browser visit, “Source behavior (S12, not executed)” is selected with Escrow funding 110 CASH, Cash remaining 73, and a 2 CASH backing gap. The proposed button changes the live state to 112. Both states are clearly described once read, but the supplied screenshot does not identify itself as the proposed state.

evidence.freshBrowserDefault: #worksheet at 35; source mode; funding 110; cash remaining 73; duties 75; 2 CASH backing gap

findings.suggestedChange: Label the section screenshot as the proposed 112 state or update it to match the fresh page default; make the selected mode visible in any screenshot used as the worksheet preview.

teachBack: I understand a Web as the proposed set of proof requirements a consuming contract needs for one transition, and a Strand as one proof with its claim, statement and binding details. Here the worksheet demonstrates arithmetic: paying 35 from a 100 invoice leaves 65 invoice duty plus the 10 reserve, or 75 duties; the 2 fee does not pay the invoice. Source funding is 110 and leaves 73 after that partial, so it is 2 short of the remaining duties. The proposed 112 policy adds 2 for this one partial, but the page says that amount is not an S12 source action and more partials need another fee allowance. The page describes scoped local test records, while saying these illustrations do not run proofs, signatures or transactions and no on-chain transaction is recorded. I take the page’s maturity panel as a description of supplied records, not as something this payer review independently verifies.
limits: This is a bounded role-play review, not real human research.
I used only the frozen local HTML, named screenshots, required workflow materials and rendered page behavior; I did not inspect source code or use external navigation.
I made no security, cryptographic correctness, ledger acceptance or financial advice judgment.
The page and arithmetic claims are reported as shown; I did not independently recompute against source material.
